# v1.1.0-dev.75 — The right pane takes the keyboard

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.74`.

## You Can Actually Use The Right Pane Without A Mouse

Tab moved focus to the windows pane and then nothing happened. The
footer said **j/k — windows**, which was true in the visual editor and
had never been true in list view — the default view. So the pane took
focus, showed no cursor, and every key either fired a profile-level
action or did nothing at all.

List view has the same motions the canvas has always had:

- <kbd>j</kbd> / <kbd>k</kbd> move the cursor down and up
- <kbd>gg</kbd> and <kbd>G</kbd> jump to the first and last window
- <kbd>Enter</kbd> (or <kbd>e</kbd>) edits the window under the cursor
- <kbd>x</kbd> removes it

Tab into the pane and the cursor lands on a row rather than nowhere, so
it's obvious the pane is listening. <kbd>h</kbd> and <kbd>l</kbd> still
reach history and load — the cursor keys only claim the keys they
actually use.

The help overlay (<kbd>?</kbd>) lists all of these now. It never
mentioned them before, because they didn't exist.

## Dialogs Read As Dialogs

A distinct border around every dialog window, and a shadow under it, so
it separates from whatever is behind it instead of blending into the
desktop.

The gap between a dialog and the app window behind it has doubled —
50px on every side rather than 25 — so more of the app stays visible
around it. Dialogs are still resizable windows, so that's a starting
point rather than something you're stuck with.

## The Display Editor Lost Its Summary Strip

The "When you press…" block at the top of the display dialog is gone.
The controls under it already say what they do, and it cost a fixed
slab of height at the top of every display dialog.

What it said still reaches screen readers, which is the part worth
keeping — the plan is genuinely useful to hear as settings change.

With that space freed, the monitor panel now fills the dialog instead
of scrolling inside a fixed fraction of it. Before this, the card was
cut off mid-way with a third of the dialog sitting empty underneath.

## A Bug Worth Naming

Deleting the summary's stylesheet rules line by line stripped two
selectors and left their declaration bodies behind. Orphaned
declarations break the rule that follows them, and what followed was
the rule that hides screen-reader-only text — so the announcement that
was supposed to be invisible rendered as a visible paragraph at the top
of the dialog.

The check that was supposed to catch it excluded screen-reader elements
by their class, so it passed while the thing was plainly on screen. It
asks for the rendered box now instead of trusting the markup.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
